items.title: Ship bundled vendor price seed table for fresh installs
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a bundled table of confirmed vendor prices (`AuctionatorVendorSeed.lua`) to seed fresh installs with server-deterministic pricing facts, reducing reliance on the estimator's `est` tier (which has ~20% median error). Includes the integration plan (`VENDOR-SEED-PLAN.md`) and corrected accuracy documentation.

## Changes

- **`AuctionatorVendorSeed.lua`** (new, auto-generated)
  - 774 confirmed sale observations (`obs` table): `itemID:ilvl:req` → copper price
  - 344 trusted base facts (`base` table): `itemID` → `{price, ilvl, req}`
  - Metadata: build timestamp, observation/base counts, source dump ID
  - ~35 KB, parses under `luac5.1 -p`
  - Server-deterministic facts only (no local cache state)

- **`VENDOR-SEED-PLAN.md`** (new)
  - Execution plan for integrating the seed into `AuctionatorHints.lua`
  - Five steps: load seed file, merge at login (non-destructive), tag seed predictions, optional tooltip provenance, surface in diagnostics
  - Detailed code snippets for each integration point with line-number anchors
  - Explains the measurement strategy: seed-only tuples tagged `pt = "seed"` on first real sale to measure shipped-table accuracy

- **`VENDOR-PRICE.md`** (updated)
  - Corrected accuracy section: offline replay (4.1%) was in-sample artifact
  - Live calibration on 500-row dump: ~10% median (all predictions), ~18% (novel instances)
  - Clarifies that `est` tier dominates at ~20% error and shape-refit is a dead end
  - Marks the active plan as shipping confirmed prices, not refitting

## Rationale

Live calibration revealed the shipped estimator's honest accuracy is ~10–18%, not the 4.1% claimed by offline replay (which leaked by scoring against the current `.obs` table). The `est` tier accounts for 75% of predictions at ~20% error and is structurally floored. Shipping a bundled table of confirmed prices allows fresh installs to resolve via `learned`/`interp` tiers (0–3% error) instead, with measurable payoff tracked via the `seed` prediction tier.

## Next steps

Integration into `AuctionatorHints.lua` follows the five-step plan in `VENDOR-SEED-PLAN.md`. The seed file is ready to load; no further generation is needed.

items.title: docs: update README with corrected accuracy numbers and storage framing
Correct the SHT4x and SCD4x accuracy figures
items.body:
Closes the two datasheet follow-ups left open in the body of PR #140.

## SHT4x humidity accuracy

ADR-0014 d4 stated ±1.5 %RH for the SHT45 — a figure matching no member of the family.

| Part | RH accuracy (typ) |
|------|-------------------|
| SHT40 | ±1.8 %RH |
| SHT41 | ±1.8 %RH |
| SHT45 | ±1.0 %RH |

The figure is **removed from the ADR rather than corrected**. Accuracy is a concrete part value, and ADR-0000 d2 puts concrete values in the document whose job that value is, with d3 forbidding a second copy. Mirroring it into ADR-0014 is what allowed it to drift and then propagate. No decision changes, so no revision is bumped — same handling as the ADR-0017 editorial sweep in 1388cdf.

The wrong figure had been copied into two further documents:

| Document | Designator | Was | Now |
|----------|-----------|-----|-----|
| `spec/M06-VENTILATION` | U4 | ±1.5 %RH (`verify`) | ±1.0 %RH typ (`verify`) |
| `spec/M07-AMBIENT` | U1 | ±1.5 %RH (`verify`) | ±1.0 %RH typ (`verify`) |

Both keep the `verify` marker; those specs are pre-schematic. M01 already carried ±1.0 %RH typ, so the VPD budget in its §6.1 is unaffected — that section now also records that ADR-0014 d4 states no accuracy for U1.

## SCD4x CO₂ accuracy

Checked against Sensirion SCD4x datasheet **version 1.5 (July 2023), table 1**.

M01's `±(50 ppm + 2.5 % of reading)` at 400–1000 ppm **is correct**. The `±(50 ppm + 5 %)` it replaced is the **SCD40** row; M01 populates an SCD41. The proportional term was not halved in error.

M01 gains the full banded figure, because its expected range includes night accumulation, which crosses the 1000 ppm band edge:

| Band | SCD41 accuracy |
|------|----------------|
| 400–1000 ppm | ±(50 ppm + 2.5 % of reading) |
| 1001–2000 ppm | ±(50 ppm + 3 % of reading) |
| 2001–5000 ppm | ±(40 ppm + 5 % of reading) |

Datasheet default conditions — 25 °C, 50 %RH, 1013 mbar, periodic measurement, 3.3 V — are recorded with the figure. The SCD40 value is named as the SCD40's, so the same substitution cannot recur.

`spec/M07-AMBIENT` carried the SCD40 figure against an SCD41 and is corrected to the two bands its 400–1200 ppm expected range spans. Its CO₂ range and accuracy drop the `verify` marker.

## Not changed

M01 §6.3.1 already disables ASC and mandates FRC, which is the correct reading of datasheet footnotes 1 and 4 (sub-400 ppm exposure degrades accuracy while ASC is on; ASC needs weekly 400 ppm exposure a closed cabinet need not reach). No open item is opened or closed by this PR.

Text sharing a block with a fence bypassed escaping `processBlock()` detected the fenced-code placeholder with `startsWith()`, a prefix test. `splitBlocks()` splits on blank lines, so a fence *not* followed by a blank line left the placeholder and the text after it in a single block — and that whole block was returned early, reaching the output without ever passing through `escapeHtml()`: ```` in : ```\nc\n```\n out: 
c
\n ```` Adding a blank line after the fence escaped the same input correctly. **This was not exploitable**: the downstream `sanitizeHtml()` tag/attribute allowlist drops the markup that lands in the output. But it made the sanitizer the *only* defense rather than the second layer the module header describes, so the header comment was false as written and is corrected here. `splitBlocks()` now splits at placeholder boundaries as well, so a placeholder always stands alone in its own block, and `processBlock()` matches the whole block instead of a prefix. Splitting — rather than only tightening the test — keeps adjacent fences with no blank line between them rendering as sibling `
` elements; text around a fence is now escaped and inline-processed like any other paragraph, and a fence followed by a blank line is unaffected.

Step 1 also strips NUL from the input. Placeholders are the only strings that bypass escaping, so input must not be able to forge one: a hand-written NUL-delimited `CODEBLOCK0` placeholder followed by markup, with no fence present at all, reproduced the same raw passthrough on its own.

## Tests

`src/test/js/themes/bootstrap/markdown.test.js` gains 12 cases. 8 of them fail against the pre-fix renderer:

```
Tests  8 failed | 30 passed (38)
```

and the full suite passes with the fixes:

```
Test Files  17 passed (17)
     Tests  448 passed (448)
```

Assertions are on the full output string rather than substring containment, so a partial restore cannot pass. The remaining 4 cases guard behaviour the fix must not regress (`$1` with no capture group; adjacent fences still rendering as siblings).

## Notes

- The two fix commits predate #3194/#3195 and were rebased onto current master; the only conflict was the module header comment, resolved to keep master's "static theme SPA" wording with the corrected accuracy claim.

items.title: docs(concepts): explain the installer types (.msi / .exe / .msix|.appx)
items.body:
Adds an **Installer types** section to `concepts.md` explaining how `.msi`, `.exe`, and `.msix`/`.appx` each behave — what you must supply, how each installs, and where its uninstall comes from.

## The bit the docs never said

**`.exe` is the only type whose uninstall depends on the sandbox capture.** An MSI is removed by PSADT Zero-Config from the MSI itself; an MSIX by its package identity, read from the manifest at configure time. Both work even if a capture finds nothing. That framing makes the recent MSIX work make sense, and it was nowhere in the docs.

| | `.msi` | `.exe` | `.msix` / `.appx` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installs via | PSADT Zero-Config | your silent switches | provisioning (SYSTEM) / `Add-AppxPackage` (interactive) |
| Silent switches | not needed | **required** | not applicable |
| Uninstall from | the MSI itself | **the capture** | the package manifest |
| Needs the capture | no | **yes** | no |

## Things admins get bitten by, now written down

- **The `/S` guess is silent.** A winget EXE with no `InstallerSwitches.Silent` gets `/S` with no warning — right for NSIS, wrong for Inno (`/VERYSILENT`). The manifest's `InstallerType` isn't consulted. Fix it in `AppConfig.json`; it's data, not code.
- **Advanced/"hard" mode is manual-only** — a winget EXE never becomes one.
- **MSIX must be signed** or Windows won't install it, even via Intune. winget packages are CA-signed (nothing to do); your own LOB package needs its cert in **Local Computer – Trusted People**, delivered *before* the app. (Verified against Microsoft Learn — the Intune-specific guidance differs from the generic sideload page's "Trusted Root".)
- **Detection needs an org template.** The tattoo requires an app-script author, which only a template supplies. Without it the toolkit falls back to capture-based rules — which find nothing for MSIX, so a package can publish with **no detection rule**. The publish warning is non-blocking: the app is created regardless.
- **Bundles**: the extension lies (winget names a `.msixbundle` `.msix`), so detection is by content.

## Drive-by corrections

Two claims went stale when the icon precedence gained a template tier (#41), plus one wrong code comment:

- The icon list implied winget `IconUrl` outranks `-IconPath`. They **never compete** — mutually exclusive entry points, both authoritative — so they're now one tier. Adds the org-template logo tier (gated on `CustomAssets`) and the PSADT default.
- The 48px rule is **capture-only**, and the `.exe` parenthetical was **backwards**: `.exe` icons are rendered at 256×256 and *can* be upscaled. Also notes a captured icon never helps an MSIX (no ARP entry to read).
- `manual-apps.md`: "Nothing extra" → "Nothing to author", with the MSIX signing prerequisite called out; the uninstall sentence no longer implies MSI uses the capture.
- `Add-Win32ToolkitTemplateAssets`: a comment claimed `-IconPath` is stamped *before* Apply. It isn't — Apply runs first and the `Copy-Item -Force` is what wins. Outcome unchanged, reasoning corrected.

## Accuracy

Every claim was fact-checked against the code by two adversarial passes, which caught **12 inaccuracies in my drafts** — including "MSI uninstall comes from the capture" (it doesn't), an invented "the toolkit tells you it guessed `/S`" (it doesn't), and advice to "not publish past that warning" (impossible — it fires after the upload begins).

Docs-only apart from one comment; CI runs the strict site build and the link/anchor check.

items.title: fix(gateway,agent): arm orphan watchdog for late-registered spans (#605) + cancel-fallback empty-session guard; widen flaky budgets (#606)

labels.name: area:gateway
labels.description: pkg/gateway/* — HTTP API, WS, auth, CORS, routing

items.body:
## What

Three fixes riding one branch off the release tip:

1. **#605 — orphan watchdog arming race (real product bug).** The root `TurnEnd` and a delegate's `SubTurnSpawn` are emitted from different goroutines, so a spawn event can reach the WS event forwarder after the root turn_end. The `TurnEnd` case only arms spans already registered in `openSpans`; a span registered later was never armed — no reschedule ceiling, no forced `subagent_end{interrupted}`, a subagent stuck "running" in the UI forever. Fix: the forwarder latches root-turn-ended state (+ watchdog reason), arms late registrations immediately at `SubTurnSpawn`, and resets the latch only on a ROOT `TurnStart` (`TurnStartPayload` gains `IsRoot`, internal event only — no wire change) so a child's own turn-start cannot reopen the hole for a later-arriving sibling spawn. This race is what actually failed both Linux legs of cross-platform run 31184159924 on PR #604 (a diff with zero gateway code).

2. **Cancel descendant-fallback empty-sessionID guard (14-reviewer sign-off finding, cancel-cascade lens, MEDIUM).** The merge restoration (7f4eab0b) of the cancel fallback kept the correct `!armed` addition but dropped the base's `sessionID != ""` half. Turns with an empty `routingSessionID` legally exist, and a Tier B cancel in an idle chat resolves to `""` — the unguarded fallback then claims an arbitrary unrelated empty-routing-id turn, consuming its first-cancel-wins latch and reporting `fired=true` for a cancel that reached nothing. Guard restored at both layers (RequestCancel gate + `claimAnyTurnForSession` early return), plus the stale doc header and FR-014 reader-census prose corrected (docs-accuracy lens findings 1/2/4).

3. **#606 — flaky-test budget widens.** `browser_webrtc_fixwavea_test.go` `fenceBudget` 2s→10s (the budget bounds a path with 20s internal ceilings; a genuine regression of the fence fix blocks forever, so any finite budget still discriminates) and the orphan-liveness frame deadline 5s→15s (nominal ~200ms). No assertion weakened.

## Test evidence

- 3 new forwarder-level regression tests (`orphan_watchdog_late_spawn_test.go`): spawn-after-turn-end arms + interrupts; new ROOT turn-start resets the latch; a CHILD turn-start does NOT reset it (the sibling hole). RED-proven against the pre-fix forwarder: 2/3 fail exactly as the bug predicts, all pass with the fix.
- New `TestClaimAnyTurnForSession_EmptySessionID_NeverClaimsEmptyRoutingTurn`: RED-proven against the unguarded function, green with the guard.
- Scoped local runs green (`go vet` both packages; watchdog + forwarder + cancel-fallback test sets).

Closes #605, closes #606.

(Note: base is the non-default release branch, so auto-close will not fire — the issues will be closed manually with a comment citing this PR after merge.)

items.title: docs: republish accuracy from the corrected estimator, and retire a claim
items.body:
Two training runs have landed since [#404](https://github.com/kristenmartino/gridpulse/pull/404) fixed ledger-23, so the published accuracy numbers can be **replaced with measured ones** instead of carrying a warning that they are wrong.

Regenerated from production GCS metas at `latest.json`, 2026-08-07, all 51 regions — **all 51 reporting `scored="out_of_sample"`**.

| Statistic | XGBoost-only | Best-base per BA | Ensemble (served) |
|---|---|---|---|
| min | 1.89% (ERCOT) | 1.72% (ERCOT) | 1.38% (SPP) |
| median | 3.69% | 3.69% | **4.35%** |
| mean | 5.37% | 4.95% | **6.27%** |
| p90 | 9.87% | 9.87% | **14.27%** |
| max | 37.50% (SPA) | 23.26% (SPA) | **30.86%** (IID) |

## Two changes moved this table, and they are separable

The base columns come from `_holdout_metrics_*`, which ledger-23 **never touched** — they moved purely from a month of retraining. Only the ensemble column carries the bias correction, and it was measured on the *same* run with the old estimator logged beside the new:

| ensemble median | |
|---|---|
| previously published (2026-07-03, in-sample) | 4.82% |
| 2026-08-07, in-sample — what the old code would say today | 3.89% |
| **2026-08-07, out-of-sample — published** | **4.35%** |

Retraining bought **−0.93 pts**; the correction gave back **+0.46**. Both are in the docs; neither is presented as the whole story.

The correction is **far larger in the tail than at the median** — mean +1.32 against median +0.46, worse on 33 of 51 BAs. That is the shape you would expect: in-sample weighting has most to exploit where models disagree most.

## A claim is withdrawn, not restated

Both docs argued the ensemble earns its keep as *variance-reduction on the tail*, resting on **SEC 38.63% → 13.61%**. On 2026-08-07 SEC is XGBoost **13.68%** and ensemble **14.72%** — the blend is *worse* there. Ensemble p90 (14.27%) is now well above XGBoost-only’s (9.87%).

I did not hunt for a replacement example. A claim that needs a freshly-chosen example every retrain was never a claim. The honest statement is that the blend buys error decorrelation on some BAs and costs accuracy on others, and only the per-BA table says which.

## Consequences of the same table, also corrected

- Best base is XGBoost on **42 of 51**, not 44 — and **which model wins a BA is not stable across retrains**: only SEC and SC held their column since July. Called out explicitly, because citing a BA’s champion from memory is now a trap.
- Ensemble beats XGBoost-alone on **21 of 51**, not 17 (`HOW_IT_WORKS`, `INTERVIEW_PREP`, `README`).
- README’s XGBoost line: 42 of 51, ERCOT 1.89%, median 3.69%.
- The 51-row per-BA table in `BACKTEST_RESULTS` regenerated from the same pull.

## Notes

`docs/_holdout_table.md` was regenerated locally and matches `BACKTEST_RESULTS` **row-for-row on all 51 BAs (0 mismatches, verified)** — but is **not in this commit**: it is gitignored as a regenerable artifact, which is right for a file that goes stale every training run.

Five references to `2026-07-03` survive on purpose — each is explicitly the older measurement being compared against, not a live figure.

## Explanatory-doc check

- Architecture changed? No.
- Cited fact moved? **Yes** — `CANONICAL_FACTS` accuracy block updated here, in the same commit as its consumers.
- STAR-story trigger? The arc belongs at #273 close.
- `STATUS.md`? No change to active focus.

Docs-only.

A batch of ten small, independently-verified fixes found by auditing the R modules. Each was checked against a concrete failing input and against the existing tests. No new dependencies.

## Correctness (behavioural)

1. **BRFSS `CHILDREN == 88` ("none") was coerced to `NA`** (`R/data-urps_population.R`). The comment says 88 = none, but the code lumped it with 99 (refused) → every zero-parity woman dropped from `mean_children` (`NaN` for all-childless cells, upward-biased parity elsewhere). Now `88 → 0`, `99 → NA`. The test helper that mirrors this coding is updated too.
2. **Income tier off-by-one** (`R/data-urps_population.R`). BRFSS `INCOME3` code 9 is \$100–150k (six figures) but was bucketed `50k_100k`; `GT100k` started at code 10. Now `7:8 → 50k_100k`, `9:11 → GT100k`.
3. **`shift_retirement_schedule(delta < 0)` built a descending range** (`R/supply-provider_lifecycle.R`). `RETIREMENT_MIN_AGE:(min-1)` = `50:49` injected a spurious age-49 hazard and a duplicate age-50 filler that masked the real shifted hazard. Guarded so the young-end gap fills only when retiring later.
4. **`build_urps_exit_hazard()` split its message across two `sprintf()` strings** (`R/supply-retirement_hazard.R`). Only the first (no `%`) was the format, so the Weibull `scale_shift` line was dropped and `sprintf` warned. Merged into one format string.
5. **`abs_pct_error` divided by `observed` without the `observed > 0` guard** its sibling `ratio` column has (`R/calibration-demand_lifecourse.R`) → a zero-observed category made `summary$mape` `Inf` (`na.rm` does not drop `Inf`). Guarded to `NA_real_`.
6. **`calculate_state_vulnerability()` ranked by the wrong column** (`R/reporting-workforce_statistics.R`). It computed a `log10(active)`-weighted `vulnerability_score` (its whole documented purpose) then sorted by the *unweighted* `pct_loss_if_retire`. Now ranks by `vulnerability_score`; the self-contradictory test (titled "weighted by log active count" but asserting the unweighted winner) is corrected.

## Documentation accuracy

7. **Age-band doc** (`R/data-urps_population.R`) claimed the top bands align with mufflyaccess `(65-79, 80+)`; the actual bands and the `AGEG5YR` crosswalk are `(65-74, 75+)`. Corrected the claim to match the data.

items.title: fix: entity.ValidateRecord's Required check rejects whitespace-only strings
items.body:
Closes universaltill/uc-infra#105.

## What

`entity.ValidateRecord`'s `Required` check rejected an empty string (`""`) since uc-infra#86, but not a whitespace-only one (`"   "`). `internal/kernel/csvimport.buildRowData` already trims a CSV cell before building the row, so a whitespace-only CSV cell was treated as blank/absent — but a direct JSON API POST could still create a record with a Required field set to `"   "`. The two entry points disagreed about what "blank" means for the identical Definition.

New, exported `entity.IsBlankString(v any) bool` is the shared "is this string blank" definition; `ValidateRecord`'s `Required` check now uses it instead of the old `v == ""` comparison. Deliberately narrow scope, matching #86's own precedent: Required strings only, not a general behavior change — `FieldI18nText`'s own separate whitespace-counts-as-content rule is untouched by design.

## Independent review findings, all fixed here

An opus-model independent review of the first draft found the widening needed to propagate further than just the one check:

- **`internal/data.RecordRepo.CountMissingField`'s SQL** still matched only literal `""`, silently under-reporting whitespace-only legacy rows in `cmd/sync-tenant-modules`' migration-readiness report. Fixed with an explicit-charset `btrim`.
- **`internal/kernel/crud.uniqueKeyValue`** had its own copy of the "blank" check (kept in sync with `Required` since uc-infra#81's fix for plain `""`), which had silently fallen out of sync again for whitespace. Now calls `entity.IsBlankString` directly instead of duplicating the definition.
- **Test coverage** was entity-unit-only; #86's own precedent for the identical check shipped crud-integration, real-HTTP-API, and real-browser E2E layers too (the review also flagged that whitespace is a *newly* browser-reachable round trip — HTML5 `required` is satisfied by whitespace, so no JS stripping is needed to reach the server, unlike the `""` case). All four layers now covered.
- **`internal/kernel/finance/basecurrency_test.go`'s** whitespace-only malformed-code case was restored (seeded directly via the repo, bypassing validation) rather than deleted, matching the precedent `internal/api/saftexport_test.go` set for the identical "guard is write-path only, legacy rows still exist" situation.
- A couple of doc comments corrected for accuracy/staleness.

One narrow finding — a hidden-from-actor field carrying a legacy whitespace-only Required value blocks every save of that record — is a genuine product/UX decision, not defaulted past here; split out to universaltill/uc-infra#178.

Full review record: `uc-infra/docs/code-reviews/2026-08-07-whitespace-only-required-fields.md` (private repo).

## Testing

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all clean. Full `go test ./... -p 1` against a real local Postgres — every package green, including `internal/e2e`'s real headless-Chrome tests. Whole-program coverage (CI's `-coverpkg` scope) 85.3%, floor 83.5%.

Test-first: new entity-layer assertions were confirmed failing against the pre-fix code, then passing after. The crud/API/E2E/data-layer additions are new coverage the review flagged as missing for already-shipped-and-verified behavior.
